chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Fuzalat ibn Ayoob, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Abi Zyad, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them).
He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Whoever wishes for something while God is pleased with him, he will not leave this world until he is granted it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a wish to be granted by God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to illustrate the efficacy of *tamanni* (sincere wishing) as a spiritual mechanism that bridges human intent with divine will. It underscores the Shia concept that a desire becomes a guaranteed reality when it is not merely a personal whim but is rooted in and pleasing to Allah, reflecting the harmony between human agency and divine decree.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-7 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Fuzalat ibn Ayoob, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Abi Zyad , on the authority of Aba Abdullah - Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (MGB)
that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “If one wants something and the Almighty God is pleased with him, then God will not take him out of this world until He grants it to him.”
